questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider the series of reactions given and identify the final product [Z].
questions.solution:
The starting material is 2-methylpropan-2-ol. Treatment with 20% $H_3PO_4$ causes acid-catalyzed dehydration to form 2-methylpropene [W].

$(CH_3)_3C-OH \xrightarrow{H^+} (CH_3)_2C=CH_2$

Next, 2-methylpropene [W] undergoes hydroboration-oxidation with $(BH_3)_2$ in THF followed by $H_2O_2 / NaOH$. This results in the anti-Markovnikov addition of water, yielding the primary alcohol 2-methylpropan-1-ol [X].

$(CH_3)_2C=CH_2 \xrightarrow{(i) (BH_3)_2, (ii) H_2O_2/OH^-} (CH_3)_2CH-CH_2-OH$

Oxidation of the primary alcohol 2-methylpropan-1-ol [X] with $CrO_3$ yields the corresponding aldehyde, 2-methylpropanal [Y].

$(CH_3)_2CH-CH_2-OH \xrightarrow{CrO_3} (CH_3)_2CH-CHO$

Finally, 2-methylpropanal [Y] reacts with the Grignard reagent methylmagnesium bromide ($CH_3MgBr$) followed by hydrolysis to form the secondary alcohol 3-methylbutan-2-ol [Z].

$(CH_3)_2CH-CHO \xrightarrow{(i) CH_3MgBr, (ii) H_2O} (CH_3)_2CH-CH(OH)-CH_3$

The structure of 3-methylbutan-2-ol corresponds to the fourth option.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An unsaturated organic compound (C_3$H_6$), undergoes the following series of reactions:
$\text{C}_3\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow{\large{dil\ H_2SO_4}} [\text{B}]\ (\text{Major Product}) \xrightarrow{\large{+\ HCl\ /\ ZnCl_2}} [\text{C}] \xrightarrow{\large{Na_{(s)}\ /\ dry\ ether}} [\text{D}]$
Identify compound [D]
questions.solution:
The unsaturated organic compound $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$ is propene, $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$.

Hydration of propene with dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ follows Markovnikov's rule to give propan-2-ol as the major product [B].
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_3$

Reaction of propan-2-ol with Lucas reagent ($\text{HCl} / \text{ZnCl}_2$) gives 2-chloropropane [C].
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{HCl} / \text{ZnCl}_2} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH(Cl)}-\text{CH}_3$

Wurtz reaction of 2-chloropropane with sodium in dry ether gives 2,3-dimethylbutane [D].
$2\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(Cl)}-\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{Na} / \text{dry ether}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\text{CH(CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$

Compound [D] is 2,3-dimethylbutane.

Answer: 2,3–dimethylbutane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements [A] and [B] are given below. Choose the correct option.
A) Protonated R$-$CH_2-$OH can serve as Electrophiles while neutral R$-$OH acts as a Nucleophile. \\ B) The bond between O$-$H cleaves when R$-$CH_2-$OH acts as Electrophiles and the bond between C$-$O cleaves when they act as Nucleophiles.
options: Both the statements [A] and [B] are wrong
Statement [A] is correct but [B] is wrong
Both the statements [A] and [B] are correct
Statement [B] is correct but [A] is wrong
questions.solution:
Alcohols can act as both nucleophiles and electrophiles.

Neutral alcohols act as nucleophiles due to the presence of lone pairs of electrons on the oxygen atom. In these reactions, the O$-$H bond is cleaved.

Protonated alcohols act as electrophiles because protonation makes the hydroxyl group a good leaving group (H_2$O). In these reactions, a nucleophile attacks the carbon atom, and the C$-$O bond is cleaved. \\ \\ Statement [A] is correct as protonated R$-$CH_2-$OH acts as an electrophile and neutral R$-$OH acts as a nucleophile.

Statement [B] is incorrect because the C$-$O bond cleaves when alcohols act as electrophiles, and the O$-$H bond cleaves when they act as nucleophiles.

Answer: Statement [A] is correct but [B] is wrong

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: Reaction of alcohols with anhydrides is carried out in the presence of small amounts of Conc. H_2$SO_4$ to remove the water formed
Relative ease of dehydration of alcohols on heating with a protic acid is Primary > Secondary > Tertiary
p– Nitrophenol is more acidic than p– Cresol
Cyclic C_4$H_7$OH exists as four structural isomers
questions.solution:
The relative ease of dehydration of alcohols on heating with a protic acid follows the order: Tertiary $ \gt $ Secondary $ \gt $ Primary. This is because the dehydration mechanism involves the formation of a carbocation intermediate, and the stability of carbocations follows the order $3^{\circ} \gt 2^{\circ} \gt 1^{\circ}$. Therefore, the given statement regarding the ease of dehydration is incorrect.

The reaction of alcohols with carboxylic acids and acid anhydrides is carried out in the presence of a small amount of concentrated $H_2SO_4$. The reaction is reversible, and the removal of water drives the equilibrium forward, making the first statement contextually accepted as per standard textbook language.

In p-nitrophenol, the $-NO_2$ group is strongly electron-withdrawing ($-M$ and $-I$ effects), which stabilizes the conjugate base and increases acidity. In p-cresol, the $-CH_3$ group is electron-donating ($+I$ and hyperconjugation), which destabilizes the conjugate base. Hence, p-nitrophenol is more acidic than p-cresol.

The formula $C_4H_7OH$ has a degree of unsaturation of $1$. The possible cyclic structural isomers are cyclobutanol, 1-methylcyclopropan-1-ol, 2-methylcyclopropan-1-ol, and cyclopropylmethanol. This gives exactly four structural isomers.

Answer: Relative ease of dehydration of alcohols on heating with a protic acid is Primary > Secondary > Tertiary

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound [X] undergoes reactions as given. Identify compounds [C] and [D] formed in these reactions.
questions.solution:
The given starting compound is isopropyl phenyl ether, $Ph-O-CH(CH_3)_2$.

Reaction with concentrated HI leads to the cleavage of the ether. Due to the partial double bond character of the O-phenyl bond (arising from resonance), the cleavage occurs at the O-isopropyl bond. This yields phenol and isopropyl iodide.
$Ph-O-CH(CH_3)_2 + HI \rightarrow PhOH + CH_3-CH(I)-CH_3$
Since [A] is the aromatic product, [A] is Phenol and [B] is Isopropyl iodide.

Phenol [A] undergoes oxidation with acidified dichromate ($Cr_2O_7^{2-} / H^+$) to form p-benzoquinone.
Therefore, [C] is Benzoquinone.

Isopropyl iodide [B] reacts with aqueous KOH to undergo nucleophilic substitution, forming isopropyl alcohol.
$CH_3-CH(I)-CH_3 + aq. KOH \rightarrow CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3$

Isopropyl alcohol contains the $CH_3-CH(OH)-$ group, which gives a positive iodoform test when treated with $I_2$ and a base like $Na_2CO_3$. The reaction produces iodoform and the sodium salt of the corresponding carboxylic acid (sodium acetate).
$CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3 + I_2 + Na_2CO_3 \rightarrow CHI_3 + CH_3COONa$
Therefore, [D] is Iodoform.

Answer: [C]: Benzoquinone [D]: Iodoform

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Choose the correct reason:
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde is a liquid at room temperature while $p$-hydroxy-benzaldehyde is a high melting solid, because
options: p-hydroxybenzaldehyde, shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding while in o-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is stronger intermolecular hydrogen bonding
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows association of the molecules while in $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is no association among the molecules
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows only weak Vanderwal's forces of attraction while in $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is strong Vanderwal's forces of attraction in solid state
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding while in $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is no intramolecular hydrogen bonding
questions.solution:
o-hydroxybenzaldehyde exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding due to the proximity of the -OH and -CHO groups. This restricts the formation of intermolecular hydrogen bonds, resulting in weaker intermolecular forces and making it a liquid at room temperature.

In p-hydroxybenzaldehyde, the -OH and -CHO groups are far apart, so it cannot form intramolecular hydrogen bonds. Instead, it forms extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonds, leading to molecular association and a high melting point, making it a solid.

Thus, o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding while p-hydroxybenzaldehyde does not.

Answer: o-hydroxybenzaldehyde shows intramolecular hydrogen bonding while in $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde there is no intramolecular hydrogen bonding

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct statement?
options: Acetone undergoes reaction in presence of Ba(OH)_2$ on heating to form 4–Methylpent–3–en–2–one$
Acetophenone cannot be prepared on reacting Benzoyl chloride with Dimethyl cadmium in ether solvent
Acetophenone on reaction with I_2$ / Na_2$CO_3$ (aq) does not undergo any reaction due to the presence of deactivating $-$COCH_3$ group
Acetone reacts with NH_2-$NH_2$ / KOH in Glycol on heating to form the saturated hydrocarbon, Butane
questions.solution:
Acetone (C$H_3$COCH_3$) undergoes aldol condensation in the presence of a base like Ba(OH)_2$. Two molecules of acetone condense to form diacetone alcohol, which upon heating loses a water molecule to form an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone. \\ \\ 2 CH_3$COCH_3\xrightarrow{\text{Ba(OH)}_2}$ (CH_3$)_2$C(OH)CH_2$COCH_3\xrightarrow{\Delta}$ (CH_3$)_2$C=CHCOCH_3$ + H_2$O \\ \\ The IUPAC name of the product (CH_3$)_2$C=CHCOCH_3$ is 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one (commonly known as mesityl oxide). Thus, statement (A) is correct.

For the other options:
Statement (B) is incorrect because acetophenone (PhCOCH_3$) can be prepared by the reaction of benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) with dimethyl cadmium ((CH_3$)_2$Cd). \\ \\ Statement (C) is incorrect because acetophenone contains a methyl ketone group ($-$COCH_3$) and gives a positive iodoform test with I_2$ and a base (like Na_2$CO_3$), forming a yellow precipitate of CHI_3$.

Statement (D) is incorrect because the Wolff-Kishner reduction (NH_2$NH_2$ / KOH in glycol) of acetone (a 3-carbon compound) yields propane, not butane.

Answer: Acetone undergoes reaction in presence of Ba(OH)_2$ on heating to form 4–Methylpent–3–en–2–one

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify products [P_1$] and [P_2$] formed when Benzonitrile undergoes the following reactions.
questions.solution:
1. Formation of [X]: Benzonitrile ($C_6H_5CN$) undergoes Stephen reduction when treated with $SnCl_2/HCl$ in ether, forming an imine intermediate. Subsequent acid hydrolysis ($H_3O^+$) yields benzaldehyde ($C_6H_5CHO$). Thus, [X] is benzaldehyde.

2. Formation of [P_1$]: Benzaldehyde reacts with $HCN$ to undergo nucleophilic addition, forming benzaldehyde cyanohydrin ($C_6H_5CH(OH)CN$). Acid hydrolysis ($H_3O^+$) of the nitrile group converts it into a carboxylic acid group, yielding $\alpha$-hydroxy phenylacetic acid ($C_6H_5CH(OH)COOH$). Thus, [P_1$] is $\alpha$-hydroxy phenylacetic acid.

3. Formation of [P_2$]: Benzaldehyde does not have any $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms. When treated with a concentrated base ($50\%\ NaOH$), it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction (a disproportionation reaction). Two moles of benzaldehyde react to form one mole of benzyl alcohol ($C_6H_5CH_2OH$) and one mole of sodium benzoate ($C_6H_5COO^-Na^+$), which is the salt. Thus, [P_2$] is benzyl alcohol.

Answer: [P_1$] $\alpha$–Hydroxy phenylacetic acid and [P_2$] Benzyl alcohol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the final product formed when benzenamine reacts with the given reagents in the sequential order as:
i. (CH_3-$CO )_2$O / Pyridine. \\ ii. Conc. HNO_3$ + H_2$SO_4$ & then reacted with H_3$O$^+$ \\ iii. NaNO_2$ HCl (273K) & then reacted with H_3$PO_2$(aq).$
questions.solution:
Benzenamine (aniline) reacts with acetic anhydride in the presence of pyridine to form acetanilide. This step protects the amino group and prevents polysubstitution and oxidation.

Acetanilide undergoes nitration with a mixture of concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form $p$-nitroacetanilide as the major product due to steric hindrance at the ortho position.

Hydrolysis of $p$-nitroacetanilide with $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ removes the acetyl group, yielding $p$-nitroaniline.

$p$-Nitroaniline reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $273\text{ K}$ to form $p$-nitrobenzenediazonium chloride.

Reaction of the diazonium salt with aqueous $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ (hypophosphorous acid) reduces the diazonium group, replacing it with a hydrogen atom (deamination).

The final product formed is nitrobenzene.

Answer: Nitrobenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: Aniline cannot be prepared by Phthalimide reaction
Propan–2–amine can be obtained by reacting acetoxime with Na / C_2$H_5$OH
The decreasing order of basic strength of amines in aqueous solution is Ethanamine > N,N–Dimethylaniline > Benzenamine
Fluorobenzene cannot be prepared from Benzenediazonium chloride by Sandmeyer's reaction because Fluorination of the Diazonium salt is highly endothermic in nature
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for the preparation of primary aliphatic amines. Aniline cannot be prepared by this method because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the anion formed by phthalimide. Statement A is correct.

Acetoxime is $(CH_3)_2C=NOH$. Reduction of acetoxime with $Na / C_2H_5OH$ yields propan-2-amine, $(CH_3)_2CHNH_2$. Statement B is correct.

Aliphatic amines are more basic than aromatic amines. Among aromatic amines, the $+I$ effect of two methyl groups in N,N-dimethylaniline increases the electron density on nitrogen, making it more basic than benzenamine. Thus, the basic strength order is Ethanamine $ \gt $ N,N-Dimethylaniline $ \gt $ Benzenamine. Statement C is correct.

Fluorobenzene cannot be prepared by Sandmeyer's reaction, but it is prepared by the Balz-Schiemann reaction. The reason it cannot be prepared by Sandmeyer's reaction is not because the fluorination of the diazonium salt is highly endothermic. In fact, direct fluorination is highly exothermic and violent, and $CuF$ is not effective for the Sandmeyer reaction. Therefore, the reason provided in statement D is incorrect.

Answer: Fluorobenzene cannot be prepared from Benzenediazonium chloride by Sandmeyer's reaction because Fluorination of the Diazonium salt is highly endothermic in nature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A Nitrogen containing organic compound with molecular formula C_3$H_5$N undergoes the following reactions.
C_3$H_5$N + Na / Hg in C_2$H_5$OH \rightarrow [A]
[A] + CH_3$COCl / NaOH (aq) \rightarrow [B] \\ [A] + CHCl_3$ / KOH on heating \rightarrow [C] (foul smelling compound)
Identify compounds [B] and [C]
questions.solution:
The molecular formula of the given organic compound is $C_3H_5N$. Its degree of unsaturation is $3 + 1 - \dfrac{5}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 2$.

The compound undergoes reduction to form [A], which reacts with $CHC$l_3$ and KOH to give a foul-smelling compound [C]. This is the carbylamine reaction, which is characteristic of primary amines. Thus, [A] is a primary amine.

Since [A] is a primary amine obtained by the reduction of a compound with degree of unsaturation 2, the original compound $C_3H_5N$ must be an alkyl cyanide (nitrile). Therefore, $C_3H_5N$ is propanenitrile, $CH_3-CH_2-CN$.

Reduction of propanenitrile with Na/Hg in $C_2H_5OH$ yields propan-1-amine:
$CH_3-CH_2-CN \xrightarrow{Na/Hg, C_2H_5OH} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NH_2$ ([A])

Reaction of propan-1-amine [A] with acetyl chloride ($CH_3COCl$) in the presence of NaOH (aq) results in acetylation to form N-propylacetamide:
$CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NH_2 + CH_3COCl \xrightarrow{NaOH} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NH-COCH_3 + HCl$
Thus, [B] is $CH_3-(CH_2)_2-NH-COCH_3$.

Reaction of propan-1-amine [A] with $CHCl_3$ and KOH on heating yields propyl isocyanide, which is the foul-smelling compound:
$CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NH_2 + CHCl_3 + 3KOH \xrightarrow{\Delta} CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-NC + 3KCl + 3H_2O$
Thus, [C] is $CH_3-(CH_2)_2-NC$.

Answer: [B]: CH_3-$(CH_2$)_2-$NH$-$COCH_3$ [C]: CH_3-$(CH_2$)_2-$NC

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct statement.
options: Except Glycine and Tryptophan all the other naturally occurring Amino acids are optically active
Glucose gets oxidised to Gluconic acid with B$r_2$(aq) which indicates that the carbonyl group in it is an Aldehydic group
The "D" in D(+) –glucose represents the dextrorotatory nature of Glucose and (+) stands for its configuration
During denaturation of Proteins its 3- dimensional structure is destroyed because the primary, secondary and tertiary structures get destroyed due to rise in temperature
questions.solution:
Glycine is the only naturally occurring amino acid that is optically inactive because its $\alpha$-carbon is attached to two hydrogen atoms. Tryptophan is optically active. Thus, the first statement is incorrect.

Bromine water is a mild oxidising agent that specifically oxidises aldehydes to carboxylic acids. The oxidation of glucose to gluconic acid by bromine water confirms the presence of an aldehydic group. Thus, the second statement is correct.

In D(+)-glucose, 'D' represents the relative configuration with respect to glyceraldehyde, while '(+)' represents the dextrorotatory nature of the molecule. Thus, the third statement is incorrect.

During the denaturation of proteins, the secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed due to the unfolding of the protein chain, but the primary structure (the sequence of amino acids) remains intact. Thus, the fourth statement is incorrect.

Answer: Glucose gets oxidised to Gluconic acid with B$r_2$(aq) which indicates that the carbonyl group in it is an Aldehydic group

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A small segment of a polypeptide gave on complete hydrolysis 3 molecules of alanine, 2 molecules of glycine and 3 molecules of cysteine. What is the number of peptide linkages in the segment of the polypeptide?
questions.solution:
Total number of amino acid molecules obtained on complete hydrolysis = $3 + 2 + 3 = 8$.

In a linear polypeptide chain, the number of peptide linkages is equal to the total number of amino acid residues minus one.

Number of peptide linkages = $8 - 1 = 7$.

Answer: $7$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reagents, [A] and [B] used up when Salicylic acid undergoes the following reactions:
questions.solution:
Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) contains both a carboxylic acid group ($-\text{COOH}$) and a phenolic hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$).

In reaction [A], the $-\text{COOH}$ group is converted into an ester group ($-\text{COOCH}_3$), while the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group remains unaffected. This product is methyl salicylate (oil of wintergreen). This transformation is a Fischer esterification, which requires methanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$) in the presence of an acid catalyst ($\text{H}^+$). Thus, reagent [A] is $\dfrac{\text{CH}_3\text{OH}}{\text{H}^+}$.

In reaction [B], the phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group is acetylated to form an ester ($-\text{OCOCH}_3$), while the $-\text{COOH}$ group remains unaffected. This product is acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin). This acetylation is typically carried out using acetic anhydride ($(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}$) in the presence of an acid catalyst ($\text{H}^+$) and gentle warming. Thus, reagent [B] is $\dfrac{(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}}{\text{H}^+(warm)}$.

Comparing this with the given options, option (C) correctly identifies both reagents.

Answer: A: $\dfrac{\text{CH}_3\text{OH}}{\text{H}^+}$ B: $\dfrac{(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})_2\text{O}}{\text{H}^+(warm)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of bond pairs and lone pairs of electrons in the molecule $\text{IF}_5$ is:
questions.solution:
The central atom in $\text{IF}_5$ is Iodine (I).

Number of valence electrons in Iodine = $7$.

Number of Fluorine atoms bonded to Iodine = $5$.

Each Fluorine atom forms a single bond with Iodine, so the number of bond pairs = $5$.

Number of valence electrons used in bonding = $5$.

Remaining valence electrons on Iodine = $7 - 5 = 2$.

Number of lone pairs = $\dfrac{2}{2} = 1$.

Thus, the molecule $\text{IF}_5$ has $5$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair.

Answer: $5, 1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: According to Molecular orbital theory, which of the following is correct with respect to bond order?
options: Bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ and $\text{O}_2^+$ is less than $\text{O}_2$
Bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ is less than $\text{N}_2$ while that of $\text{O}_2^+$ is more than $\text{O}_2$.
Bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ and $\text{O}_2^+$ is more than $\text{N}_2$
Bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ is less than $\text{O}_2$ while that of $\text{O}_2^+$ is more than $\text{O}_2$.
questions.solution:
Bond order is calculated as $\dfrac{N_b - N_a}{2}$, where $N_b$ is the number of bonding electrons and $N_a$ is the number of antibonding electrons.

For $\text{N}_2$ ($14$ electrons), the molecular orbital configuration is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}{}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}{}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^2$
Bond order = $\dfrac{10 - 4}{2} = 3$

For $\text{N}_2^+$ ($13$ electrons), the configuration is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}{}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}{}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^1$
Bond order = $\dfrac{9 - 4}{2} = 2.5$
Thus, the bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ is less than that of $\text{N}_2$.

For $\text{O}_2$ ($16$ electrons), the configuration is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}{}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}{}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_x}{}^1 \pi^{*}_{2p_y}{}^1$
Bond order = $\dfrac{10 - 6}{2} = 2$

For $\text{O}_2^+$ ($15$ electrons), the configuration is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}{}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}{}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_x}{}^1$
Bond order = $\dfrac{10 - 5}{2} = 2.5$
Thus, the bond order of $\text{O}_2^+$ is more than that of $\text{O}_2$.

Answer: Bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ is less than $\text{N}_2$ while that of $\text{O}_2^+$ is more than $\text{O}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An equilibrium mixture taken in 2litre vessel of the reaction: $2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g)$ has 4 moles of $\text{SO}_2$, 3moles of $\text{O}_2$ and 6moles of $\text{SO}_3$ then the value of equilibrium constant $(K_c)$ will be:
questions.solution:
The given equilibrium reaction is:

$2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g)$

The volume of the vessel is $V = 2$ L.

The equilibrium concentrations of the gases are:

$[\text{SO}_2] = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

$[\text{O}_2] = \dfrac{3}{2} = 1.5 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

$[\text{SO}_3] = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$

The expression for the equilibrium constant $K_c$ is:

$K_c = \dfrac{[\text{SO}_3]^2}{[\text{SO}_2]^2 [\text{O}_2]}$

Substituting the equilibrium concentrations into the expression:

$K_c = \dfrac{(3)^2}{(2)^2 \times (1.5)}$

$K_c = \dfrac{9}{4 \times 1.5} = \dfrac{9}{6} = 1.5 \text{ L mol}^{-1}$

Answer: 1.5 L mol$^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When the concentration of the reactant in a given reaction is halved and if the rate of reaction is halved, the order of the reaction is:
questions.solution:
Let the rate of the reaction be $r = k[A]^n$, where $n$ is the order of the reaction.

When the concentration of the reactant is halved, the new concentration is $\dfrac{[A]}{2}$.

The new rate is given as $\dfrac{r}{2}$.

Substituting these into the rate law:

$\dfrac{r}{2} = k\left(\dfrac{[A]}{2}\right)^n$

Dividing the new rate equation by the original rate equation:

$\dfrac{\dfrac{r}{2}}{r} = \dfrac{k\left(\dfrac{[A]}{2}\right)^n}{k[A]^n}$

$\dfrac{1}{2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^n$

Comparing the powers, we get $n = 1$.

Thus, the order of the reaction is $1$.

Answer: 1

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A first order reaction is 50%complete in 30 minutes at 300 K and in 10 minutes at 320 K. The activation energy of the reaction (E_a$) is: \\ [R=8.314 J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$; log 2 = 0.3010; log 3=0.4771]$
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, the rate constant is given by $k = \dfrac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}$.

At $T_1 = 300 \text{ K}$, $k_1 = \dfrac{0.693}{30} \text{ min}^{-1}$

At $T_2 = 320 \text{ K}$, $k_2 = \dfrac{0.693}{10} \text{ min}^{-1}$

$\dfrac{k_2}{k_1} = \dfrac{30}{10} = 3$

Using the Arrhenius equation:

$\log \left( \dfrac{k_2}{k_1} \right) = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left( \dfrac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2} \right)$

$\log 3 = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 \times 8.314} \left( \dfrac{320 - 300}{300 \times 320} \right)$

$0.4771 = \dfrac{E_a}{19.147} \left( \dfrac{20}{96000} \right)$

$E_a = \dfrac{0.4771 \times 19.147 \times 96000}{20}$

$E_a = 43848 \text{ J mol}^{-1} = 43.8 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: 43.8 kJ mol$^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the synthesis of NH_3$ from H_2$ and N_2$, if $6 \times 10^{-2}$ mole of hydrogen disappears in 10 minutes, the number of moles of NH_3$ formed in 0.3 minutes is:
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the synthesis of ammonia is:

$N_2 + 3H_2 \rightarrow 2NH_3$

The rate of disappearance of $H_2$ is given by:

$-\dfrac{d[H_2]}{dt} = \dfrac{6 \times 10^{-2}}{10} = 6 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol min}^{-1}$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, the rate of formation of $NH_3$ is related to the rate of disappearance of $H_2$ as:

$\dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{d[NH_3]}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{3} \dfrac{d[H_2]}{dt}$

$\dfrac{d[NH_3]}{dt} = -\dfrac{2}{3} \dfrac{d[H_2]}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 6 \times 10^{-3} = 4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol min}^{-1}$

The number of moles of $NH_3$ formed in $0.3$ minutes is:

$\text{Moles of } NH_3 = \text{Rate} \times \text{Time} = 4 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.3 = 1.2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ moles}$

Answer: $1.2 \times 10^{-3}\ moles$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The initial pressure of the system before decomposition for a first order gas phase reaction $A_{(g)} \rightarrow B_{(g)} + C_{(g)}$ was $P_i$. After lapse of time 't', total pressure of the system increased by 'x' units and became $P_t$. The rate constant 'k' for the reaction is given as:
questions.solution:
The given gas phase reaction is $A_{(g)} \rightarrow B_{(g)} + C_{(g)}$.

At $t = 0$, the initial pressure is $P_i$.
Pressure of $A = P_i$, Pressure of $B = 0$, Pressure of $C = 0$.

At time $t$, let the pressure of $A$ decrease by $x$.
Pressure of $A = P_i - x$
Pressure of $B = x$
Pressure of $C = x$

Total pressure at time $t$ is $P_t = (P_i - x) + x + x = P_i + x$.
From this, we get $x = P_t - P_i$.

The partial pressure of reactant $A$ at time $t$ is:
$P_A = P_i - x = P_i - (P_t - P_i) = 2P_i - P_t$

For a first order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by:
$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \dfrac{P_i}{P_A}$

Substituting the value of $P_A$:
$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \dfrac{P_i}{2P_i - P_t}$

Answer: $k = \dfrac{2.303}{t}\log\dfrac{P_i}{2P_i - P_t}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following factors is altered by the addition of a catalyst during a chemical reaction?
questions.solution:
A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.

Thermodynamic state functions such as entropy, enthalpy, and internal energy depend only on the initial and final states of the system (reactants and products) and are independent of the path taken. Therefore, they remain unaffected by the addition of a catalyst.

Answer: Activation energy

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which of the following is an INCORRECT match?
options: Electron Gain enthalpy - $F \lt  Cl  \gt  Br  \gt  I$
First Ionization Enthalpies - $Na \lt  Mg  \gt  Al \lt  Si$
questions.solution:
Metallic character increases down a group and decreases from left to right across a period.

Potassium ($K$) is an alkali metal in group 1 and period 4, making it the most metallic among the given elements. Boron ($B$) is a metalloid in group 13 and period 2, making it the least metallic.

Magnesium ($Mg$) and Aluminum ($Al$) belong to period 3. Since $Mg$ is in group 2 and $Al$ is in group 13, $Mg$ is more metallic than $Al$.

The correct order of metallic character is $K \gt Mg \gt Al \gt B$.

The given order $Al \gt Mg \gt B \gt K$ is incorrect.

Answer: Metallic character - $Al \gt Mg \gt B \gt K$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the complex which exhibits all 3 characteristics; paramagnetic; high spin configuration; octahedral geometry
questions.solution:
In option (A), the complex is $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2$. The central metal ion is $\text{Co}^{3+}$, which has a $3d^6$ configuration. Since $\text{NH}_3$ acts as a strong field ligand for $\text{Co}^{3+}$, it causes pairing of electrons, resulting in a low spin, diamagnetic, and octahedral complex.

In option (B), the complex is $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$. The central metal is $\text{Ni}$ in the $0$ oxidation state, with a $3d^{10}$ configuration. It forms an $sp^3$ hybridized, tetrahedral, and diamagnetic complex.

In option (C), the complex is $[\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O})_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_2]^{2-}$. The central metal ion is $\text{Ni}^{2+}$, which has a $3d^8$ configuration. The ligands $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ are weak field ligands. The coordination number is $6$ (two from water and four from two bidentate oxalate ions), leading to an octahedral geometry. The $3d^8$ configuration in an octahedral field is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^2$, which has $2$ unpaired electrons. It undergoes $sp^3d^2$ hybridization, forming an outer orbital (high spin) and paramagnetic complex.

In option (D), the complex is $[\text{Co(NH}_3)(\text{Cl})(\text{en})_2]^{2+}$. The central metal ion is $\text{Co}^{3+}$ ($3d^6$). The presence of strong field ligands like ethylenediamine ($\text{en}$) and $\text{NH}_3$ causes electron pairing, resulting in a low spin, diamagnetic, and octahedral complex.

Therefore, only $[\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O})_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_2]^{2-}$ exhibits all three characteristics: paramagnetic, high spin configuration, and octahedral geometry.

Answer: $[\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O})_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_2]^{2-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following complex-isomerism pair matches correctly?
options: $[\text{CrCl}_2(ox)_2]^{3-}$ - Exhibits cis- trans isomerism and cis isomer is optically active
$[\text{PtCl}_2(\text{NH}_3)_2]$ - Exhibits both cis- trans and optical isomerism
$[\text{Cr(C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}$ - Exhibits cis- trans isomerism but is optically inactive
$[\text{Fe(CN)}_4(\text{NH}_3)_2]^-$ - Exhibits cis- trans isomerism and both exhibit optical isomerism
questions.solution:
$[\text{CrCl}_2(ox)_2]^{3-}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $[M(AA)_2a_2]$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism, existing as cis and trans isomers.

The trans isomer has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive.

The cis isomer lacks any plane or center of symmetry and is optically active, existing as a pair of enantiomers.

$[\text{PtCl}_2(\text{NH}_3)_2]$ is a square planar complex of the type $[Ma_2b_2]$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans) but is optically inactive due to the presence of a molecular plane of symmetry.

$[\text{Cr(C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]^{3-}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $[M(AA)_3]$. It does not exhibit geometrical isomerism but is optically active.

$[\text{Fe(CN)}_4(\text{NH}_3)_2]^-$ is an octahedral complex of the type $[Ma_4b_2]$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans), but both isomers possess a plane of symmetry and are optically inactive.

Answer: $[\text{CrCl}_2(ox)_2]^{3-}$ - Exhibits cis- trans isomerism and cis isomer is optically active

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Pick out the correct option
Assertion(A): Mercury is not considered as a transition element
Reason (R): Mercury is a liquid
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because transition elements are defined as elements having incompletely filled d-orbitals in their ground state or in any of their common oxidation states. Mercury (Hg) has a completely filled d-orbital ($5d^{10}$) in its ground state as well as in its common oxidation states. Hence, it is not considered a transition element.

Reason (R) is true because mercury is indeed a liquid at room temperature.

However, the physical state (being a liquid) is not the reason for mercury not being classified as a transition element. The correct reason is its electronic configuration.

Therefore, both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

Answer: Both A and R are true, R is not the correct explanation of A

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following does not correctly represent the order of the property indicated against it?
questions.solution:
The magnetic moment depends on the number of unpaired electrons. The electronic configurations of the given ions are $\text{Ti}^{3+}$ ($3d^{1}$), $\text{V}^{3+}$ ($3d^{2}$), $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ ($3d^{3}$), and $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ ($3d^{4}$). The number of unpaired electrons increases from 1 to 4, so the magnetic moment increases in the order $\text{Ti}^{3+} \lt \text{V}^{3+} \lt \text{Cr}^{3+} \lt \text{Mn}^{3+}$.

The highest oxidation states shown by the elements are Ti (+4), V (+5), Cr (+6), and Mn (+7). The order $\text{Ti} \lt \text{V} \lt \text{Cr} \lt \text{Mn}$ is correct.

The melting point of transition metals depends on the strength of metallic bonding, which is related to the number of unpaired electrons. However, Mn has an anomalously low melting point due to its stable half-filled $3d^{5}$ configuration, which results in weaker interatomic interactions. The correct order of melting points is $\text{Mn} \lt \text{Ti} \lt \text{Cr} \lt \text{V}$. Thus, the given order $\text{Ti} \lt \text{V} \lt \text{Cr} \lt \text{Mn}$ is incorrect.

The second ionisation enthalpy involves the removal of an electron from the $M^{+}$ ion. The electronic configurations of the $M^{+}$ ions are $\text{Ti}^{+}$ ($3d^{2}4s^{1}$), $\text{V}^{+}$ ($3d^{3}4s^{1}$), $\text{Cr}^{+}$ ($3d^{5}$), and $\text{Mn}^{+}$ ($3d^{5}4s^{1}$). Removing an electron from $\text{Cr}^{+}$ requires breaking the highly stable half-filled $3d^{5}$ configuration, making its second ionisation enthalpy the highest among them. The correct order is $\text{Ti} \lt \text{V} \lt \text{Mn} \lt \text{Cr}$.

Answer: $\text{Ti} \lt \text{V} \lt \text{Cr} \lt \text{Mn}$ [Increasing order of melting point]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The element with the highest third ionisation enthalpy is:
questions.solution:
The electronic configurations of the given elements and their divalent ions are:

Mn (Z=25): $[Ar] 3d^5 4s^2 \rightarrow Mn^{2+}: [Ar] 3d^5$
V (Z=23): $[Ar] 3d^3 4s^2 \rightarrow V^{2+}: [Ar] 3d^3$
Fe (Z=26): $[Ar] 3d^6 4s^2 \rightarrow Fe^{2+}: [Ar] 3d^6$
Cr (Z=24): $[Ar] 3d^5 4s^1 \rightarrow Cr^{2+}: [Ar] 3d^4$

The third ionization enthalpy is the energy required to remove an electron from the $+2$ ion.

$Mn^{2+}$ has a stable half-filled $3d^5$ configuration. Removing an electron from this highly stable configuration requires a very high amount of energy.

Therefore, Manganese has the highest third ionization enthalpy among the given elements.

Answer: Manganese (Z=25)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The product and its colour when MnO_2$ is fused with KOH in presence of O_2$:
questions.solution:
When $MnO_2$ is fused with $KOH$ in the presence of an oxidizing agent like $O_2$ or $KNO_3$, it forms potassium manganate ($K_2MnO_4$).

The chemical equation for the reaction is:
$2MnO_2 + 4KOH + O_2 \rightarrow 2K_2MnO_4 + 2H_2O$

The product $K_2MnO_4$ (potassium manganate) is dark green in colour.

Answer: K_2$MnO_4$, Dark green

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is always true about a spontaneous cell reaction in a galvanic cell?
questions.solution:
For a spontaneous cell reaction, the change in Gibbs free energy must be negative, i.e., $\Delta G \lt 0$.

The relationship between $\Delta G$, the standard Gibbs free energy change $\Delta G^o$, and the reaction quotient $Q_C$ is given by:
$\Delta G = \Delta G^o + RT \ln Q_C$

At equilibrium, $\Delta G = 0$ and $Q_C = K_C$, so:
$\Delta G^o = -RT \ln K_C$

Substituting this back into the first equation, we get:
$\Delta G = -RT \ln K_C + RT \ln Q_C = RT \ln \left( \dfrac{Q_C}{K_C} \right)$

For the reaction to be spontaneous ($\Delta G \lt 0$), we must have:
$RT \ln \left( \dfrac{Q_C}{K_C} \right) \lt 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{Q_C}{K_C} \lt 1 \Rightarrow Q_C \lt K_C$

In a standard galvanic cell, the standard cell potential is positive, $E^o_{cell} \gt 0$.
Since $\Delta G^o = -nFE^o_{cell}$, a positive $E^o_{cell}$ implies that $\Delta G^o \lt 0$.

Therefore, the correct conditions are $E^o_{cell} \gt 0$, $\Delta G^o \lt 0$, and $Q_C \lt K_C$.

Answer: $E^o_{cell} \gt 0;\ \Delta G^o \lt 0;\ Q_C \lt K_C$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The $\Delta$G$^o$ for the reaction, $\text{Cd}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Zn}(s) \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Cd}(s)$ is:
$\left[E^o_{\text{Cd}^{2+}/\text{Cd}} = -0.403,\ E^o_{\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}} = -0.763\ V\right]$
questions.solution:
For the reaction $\text{Cd}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Zn}(s) \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Cd}(s)$, Zn is oxidized (anode) and $\text{Cd}^{2+}$ is reduced (cathode).

$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{\circ}_{\text{anode}}$

$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = -0.403 - (-0.763) = 0.360\text{ V}$

The number of electrons transferred in the reaction is $n = 2$.

The standard Gibbs free energy change is given by:

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -nFE^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}$

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -2 \times 96500 \times 0.360$

$\Delta G^{\circ} = -69480\text{ J} = -69.48\text{ kJ}$

Rounding to one decimal place, $\Delta G^{\circ} \approx -69.5\text{ kJ}$.

Answer: $-69.5\ kJ$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Resistance of 0.2 M solution of an electrolyte is 50 $\Omega$. The conductivity of the solution is 1.3 Sm$^{-1}$. If the resistance of 0.4 M solution of the same electrolyte is 260 $\Omega$, its molar conductivity is:
questions.solution:
The cell constant $G^*$ is given by the product of conductivity and resistance of the first solution:

$G^* = \kappa_1 \times R_1$

$G^* = 1.3\ S\ m^{-1} \times 50\ \Omega = 65\ m^{-1}$

The conductivity of the $0.4\ M$ solution, $\kappa_2$, is:

$\kappa_2 = \dfrac{G^*}{R_2} = \dfrac{65\ m^{-1}}{260\ \Omega} = 0.25\ S\ m^{-1}$

The concentration of the second solution in SI units is:

$C_2 = 0.4\ mol\ L^{-1} = 0.4 \times 10^3\ mol\ m^{-3} = 400\ mol\ m^{-3}$

The molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ is given by:

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{\kappa_2}{C_2}$

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{0.25\ S\ m^{-1}}{400\ mol\ m^{-3}} = 6.25 \times 10^{-4}\ S\ m^2\ mol^{-1}$

Answer: $6.25 \times 10^{-4}\ Sm^2mol^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Using the data given below, the strongest reducing agent is:
$E^o_{\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}/\text{Cr}^{3+}} = 1.33$ V $E^o_{\text{MnO}_4^-/\text{Mn}^{2+}} = 1.51$ V
$E^o_{\text{Cl}_2/\text{Cl}^-} = 1.36$ V $E^o_{\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}} = -0.74$ V
questions.solution:
A reducing agent undergoes oxidation. The strength of a reducing agent is directly proportional to its standard oxidation potential, which is the negative of its standard reduction potential.

The standard oxidation potentials for the given species are:
$E^o_{\text{Cr}/\text{Cr}^{3+}} = -(-0.74) = +0.74$ V
$E^o_{\text{Cl}^-/\text{Cl}_2} = -1.36$ V
$E^o_{\text{Mn}^{2+}/\text{MnO}_4^-} = -1.51$ V
$E^o_{\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}} = -1.33$ V

Since $Cr$ has the highest standard oxidation potential ($+0.74$ V), it has the greatest tendency to get oxidized. Therefore, $Cr$ is the strongest reducing agent among the given options.

Answer: $Cr$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The quantity of Ca that can be produced from molten CaCl_2$, with the same quantity of electricity (in coulombs) required to produce 4.8 g of Mg from molten MgCl_2$ is:
[Atomic mass of Mg=24 u; Atomic mass of Ca=40 u]
questions.solution:
According to Faraday's second law of electrolysis, when the same quantity of electricity is passed through different electrolytes, the masses of the substances deposited are proportional to their equivalent weights.

$\dfrac{W_{Ca}}{W_{Mg}} = \dfrac{E_{Ca}}{E_{Mg}}$

Equivalent weight of Mg, $E_{Mg} = \dfrac{24}{2} = 12$

Equivalent weight of Ca, $E_{Ca} = \dfrac{40}{2} = 20$

Given $W_{Mg} = 4.8$ g.

$\dfrac{W_{Ca}}{4.8} = \dfrac{20}{12}$

$W_{Ca} = \dfrac{20}{12} \times 4.8 = 8.0$ g

Answer: $8.0$ g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an INCORRECT statement?
options: $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ are separated by fractional distillation
In sodium nitroprusside test for Sulphur, the violet colour is due to formation of complex $\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]$
questions.solution:
Electrophiles are electron-deficient species that can accept an electron pair. While $\text{AlCl}_3$, $\text{SO}_3$, and $\text{NO}_2^+$ are electrophiles, $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ possess lone pairs of electrons on their central atoms (nitrogen and oxygen, respectively). This makes them electron-rich species, so they act as nucleophiles, not electrophiles.

Option (A) is a correct statement because fractional distillation is used to separate miscible liquids with a boiling point difference of less than $25\text{ K}$.

Option (B) is a correct statement. In the sodium nitroprusside test for sulphur, the sulphide ion reacts to form a violet-coloured complex: $\text{S}^{2-} + [\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]^{2-} \rightarrow [\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$, which corresponds to $\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]$.

Option (D) is a correct statement as all the given species have either a negative charge or lone pairs of electrons, making them nucleophiles.

Therefore, the incorrect statement is (C).

Answer: $\text{AlCl}_3, \text{NH}_3, \text{SO}_3, \text{NO}_2^+, \text{H}_2\text{O}$ are electrophiles

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the aromatic compounds among the given set based on Huckel's rule:
questions.solution:
According to Huckel's rule, a compound is aromatic if it is cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, and has $(4n + 2)\pi$ electrons, where $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$

Compound (I): Cyclopropenyl cation is cyclic, planar, and fully conjugated. It has $2\pi$ electrons. $4n + 2 = 2 \Rightarrow n = 0$. Thus, it is aromatic.

Compound (II): Naphthalene is cyclic, planar, and fully conjugated. It has $10\pi$ electrons ($5$ double bonds). $4n + 2 = 10 \Rightarrow n = 2$. Thus, it is aromatic.

Compound (III): Cyclopentadiene contains an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom, which breaks the continuous conjugation. Thus, it is non-aromatic.

Compound (IV): Azulene is cyclic, planar, and fully conjugated. It has $10\pi$ electrons ($5$ double bonds). $4n + 2 = 10 \Rightarrow n = 2$. Thus, it is aromatic.

Therefore, compounds I, II, and IV are aromatic.

Answer: I, II, IV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the given resonating structures of molecules negative mesomeric effect is represented by:
questions.solution:
The negative mesomeric effect ($-M$ effect) is observed when a substituent withdraws electron density from a conjugated system (such as a benzene ring) through resonance. This results in a decreased electron density in the ring, typically placing positive charges at the ortho and para positions.

In option (A), the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group donates a lone pair of electrons to the ring, showing a $+M$ effect and creating negative charges at the ortho and para positions.

In option (B), the $-\text{OH}$ group donates a lone pair of electrons to the ring, showing a $+M$ effect.

In option (C), the $-\text{NO}_2$ group withdraws $\pi$ electrons from the ring towards itself, creating positive charges at the ortho and para positions. This represents the $-M$ effect.

In option (D), the $-\text{NH}_2$ group donates a lone pair of electrons to the ring, showing a $+M$ effect.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct structure of o-ethyl anisole.
questions.solution:
Anisole is the common name for methoxybenzene, which consists of a benzene ring attached to a methoxy group ($-OCH_3$).

The prefix 'o-' (ortho) indicates that an ethyl group ($-C_2H_5$) is attached to the adjacent carbon atom (position 2) on the benzene ring relative to the methoxy group.

Therefore, o-ethyl anisole has an $-OCH_3$ group and a $-C_2H_5$ group at the 1 and 2 positions of the benzene ring. This structure corresponds to option (D).

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
With reference to the two statements Assertion and Reason, choose the correct option.
Assertion: The order of reactivity towards S_N$1 reaction is: C_6$H_5-$CH_2$Br > (CH_3$)_3-$C$-$Br > (CH_3$)_2-$CH$-$Br.
Reason: Among the given 3 compounds the Benzyl carbocation formed is the most stable while Isopropyl carbocation is the least stable one.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Reason is correct but Assertion is wrong
Assertion is correct but Reason is wrong
questions.solution:
The reactivity of alkyl halides towards $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ reactions depends on the stability of the intermediate carbocation formed during the rate-determining step.

The carbocations formed from the given alkyl halides are:
1. Benzyl carbocation ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2^+$) from $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$
2. tert-Butyl carbocation ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$) from $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}$
3. Isopropyl carbocation ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}^+$) from $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHBr}$

The benzyl carbocation is highly stabilized by the delocalization of the positive charge over the benzene ring through resonance. The tert-butyl carbocation is stabilized by hyperconjugation ($9\alpha$-hydrogens) and the +I effect of three methyl groups. The isopropyl carbocation is stabilized by hyperconjugation ($6\alpha$-hydrogens) and the +I effect of two methyl groups.

The resonance stabilization in the benzyl carbocation makes it the most stable among the three, while the isopropyl carbocation is the least stable.

Since the order of carbocation stability is Benzyl > tert-Butyl > Isopropyl, the order of reactivity towards $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ reaction follows the same trend: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \gt (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr} \gt (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHBr}$.

Both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the major product [Z] formed when compound [C] undergoes the following reactions:
questions.solution:
Compound [C] is 2-bromo-3-methylbutane.

Dehydrohalogenation of [C] with alcoholic KOH and heat yields the more substituted alkene (Saytzeff's rule) as the major product. Thus, [X] is 2-methylbut-2-ene, $CH_3-CH=C(CH_3)_2$.

Electrophilic addition of HCl to [X] follows Markovnikov's rule. Protonation forms the more stable tertiary carbocation, which captures a chloride ion to give 2-chloro-2-methylbutane as product [Y], $CH_3-CH_2-C(Cl)(CH_3)_2$.

Nucleophilic substitution of [Y] with alcoholic KCN yields 2,2-dimethylbutanenitrile, $CH_3-CH_2-C(CN)(CH_3)_2$.

Hydrolysis of the nitrile with dilute HCl produces 2,2-dimethylbutanoic acid as the final product [Z], $CH_3-CH_2-C(COOH)(CH_3)_2$.

This structure corresponds to the first option.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is the major product [$P_3$] formed when n- Hexane undergoes the given series of reactions: \\ $\text{n-Hexane} \xrightarrow{\large{V_2O_5;\ 20\ atm,\ 773k}} [\text{P}_1] \xrightarrow{\large{C_2H_5Cl,\ Anhyd.AlCl_3;\ \triangle}} [\text{P}_2] \xrightarrow{\large{Conc.HNO_3 + H_2SO_4;\ 333K}} [\text{P}_3]\ \text{Major product}$
\(\mathrm{n} \text {-Hexane } \frac{\mathrm{V}_2 \mathrm{O}_5}{20 \mathrm{~atm}, 773 \mathrm{k}}\left[\mathrm{P}_1\right]\)
\(\left[\mathrm{P}_1\right] \quad \xrightarrow[\triangle]{\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{Cl}, \text { Anhyd. } \mathrm{AlCl}_3}\left[\mathrm{P}_2\right]\)
\(\left[\mathrm{P}_2\right] \quad \xrightarrow[333 \mathrm{~K}]{\text { Conc. } \mathrm{HNO}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4}\left[\mathrm{P}_3\right]\) Major product
questions.solution:
The first step involves the reaction of n-hexane over $V_2O_5$ at $773$ K and $20$ atm. This is an aromatization reaction where n-hexane undergoes dehydrogenation and cyclization to form benzene. Thus, $[P_1]$ is benzene ($C_6H_6$).

The second step is the reaction of benzene ($[P_1]$) with ethyl chloride ($C_2H_5Cl$) in the presence of anhydrous $AlCl_3$ and heat. This is a Friedel-Crafts alkylation reaction. The electrophile, ethyl cation ($C_2H_5^+$), attacks the benzene ring to form ethylbenzene. Thus, $[P_2]$ is ethylbenzene ($C_6H_5CH_2CH_3$).

The third step involves the reaction of ethylbenzene ($[P_2]$) with a mixture of concentrated $HNO_3$ and concentrated $H_2SO_4$ at $333$ K. This is an electrophilic aromatic nitration. The ethyl group ($-CH_2CH_3$) attached to the benzene ring is an electron-donating group due to the $+I$ effect and hyperconjugation, making it an ortho, para-directing group. Due to the steric hindrance at the ortho position, the major product is formed by the attack of the nitronium ion ($NO_2^+$) at the para position. Therefore, the major product $[P_3]$ is p-nitroethylbenzene.

The structure of p-nitroethylbenzene matches option (2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The statements given below contains assertion and reason. Choose the correct option
Assertion (A): Propene reacts with HBr in presence of organic peroxide gives 1-bromopropane.
Reason(R): The reaction occurs through carbocation intermediate
options: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation of A
questions.solution:
Propene reacts with HBr in the presence of an organic peroxide to give 1-bromopropane. This is known as the peroxide effect or Kharasch effect, which follows anti-Markovnikov addition. Thus, the assertion is true.

The reaction proceeds via a free radical mechanism involving a more stable secondary free radical intermediate, not a carbocation intermediate. Thus, the reason is false.

Answer: A is true but R is false

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The product formed in the following reaction is:
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the addition of HBr to an alkene in the presence of benzoyl peroxide. This proceeds via a free-radical mechanism (Kharasch effect or anti-Markovnikov addition).

First, the peroxide initiates the reaction to generate a bromine radical ($Br^{\bullet}$).

The $Br^{\bullet}$ radical attacks the double bond to form the most stable carbon radical intermediate. There are two possible sites for the attack on the $HO-C_6H_4-CH=CH-CH_3$ molecule:
1. Attack at the $\alpha$-carbon gives a secondary alkyl radical: $HO-C_6H_4-CH(Br)-\dot{C}H-CH_3$
2. Attack at the $\beta$-carbon gives a benzylic radical: $HO-C_6H_4-\dot{C}H-CH(Br)-CH_3$

The benzylic radical is significantly more stable due to resonance delocalization with the benzene ring (further enhanced by the electron-donating $-OH$ group). Therefore, the $Br^{\bullet}$ radical preferentially adds to the $\beta$-carbon.

The stable benzylic radical then abstracts a hydrogen atom from another HBr molecule to yield the final product:
$HO-C_6H_4-CH_2-CH(Br)-CH_3$

Note that the phenolic $-OH$ group does not react with HBr because the aryl $C-O$ bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance and is difficult to break.

Comparing this with the given options, the correct structure is represented in option (C).

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the given alkanes in increasing order of their boiling points.
(A) 2, 2-dimethylpropane
(B) 2-methylbutane
(C) $n$-pentane
(D) $n$-butane
questions.solution:
The boiling point of alkanes increases with an increase in molecular mass due to stronger van der Waals forces. Since $n$-butane (D) has four carbon atoms while the others have five, it has the lowest boiling point.

For isomeric alkanes, the boiling point decreases with an increase in branching. Branching makes the molecule more spherical, which decreases the surface area of contact and weakens the intermolecular van der Waals forces.

Among the isomers of pentane, $n$-pentane (C) is unbranched and has the highest surface area, resulting in the highest boiling point. 2-methylbutane (B) has one branch, and 2,2-dimethylpropane (A) has two branches, making it the most spherical with the lowest boiling point among the isomers.

Thus, the increasing order of boiling points is $n$-butane (D) $\lt $ 2,2-dimethylpropane (A) $\lt $ 2-methylbutane (B) $\lt n$-pentane (C).

The correct sequence is $D \lt A \lt B \lt C$.

Answer: $D \lt A \lt B \lt C$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At 30°C the solubility of PbI_2$ salt in 0.2 M KI solution will be X, if the solubility product of PbI_2$ at 30°C is $2.4 \times 10^{-8}$. Identify the value of X.
questions.solution:
The dissociation of $PbI_2$ is given by:

$PbI_2(s) \rightleftharpoons Pb^{2+}(aq) + 2I^-(aq)$

Let the solubility of $PbI_2$ in $0.2$ M $KI$ solution be $s$.

The concentration of $I^-$ ions from $KI$ is $0.2$ M. Since $KI$ is a strong electrolyte, it completely dissociates. The total concentration of $I^-$ ions is $(2s + 0.2)$ M. Because $K_{sp}$ is very small, $2s$ can be neglected compared to $0.2$.

$[I^-] \approx 0.2$ M

The expression for the solubility product is:

$K_{sp} = [Pb^{2+}][I^-]^2$

Substituting the given values:

$2.4 \times 10^{-8} = s \times (0.2)^2$

$2.4 \times 10^{-8} = s \times 0.04$

$s = \dfrac{2.4 \times 10^{-8}}{0.04} = 6.0 \times 10^{-7}$ M

Thus, the solubility $X$ is $6.0 \times 10^{-7}$ M.

Answer: $6.0 \times 10^{-7}$M

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: x moles of $K_2$Cr_2$O_7$ oxidises 1 mole of ferrous oxalate, in acidic medium. Hence 'x' is:
questions.solution:
In acidic medium, potassium dichromate acts as an oxidizing agent and its n-factor is $6$.

$Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 14H^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2Cr^{3+} + 7H_2O$

Ferrous oxalate ($FeC_2O_4$) undergoes oxidation where both $Fe^{2+}$ and $C_2O_4^{2-}$ are oxidized.

$Fe^{2+} \rightarrow Fe^{3+} + e^-$
$C_2O_4^{2-} \rightarrow 2CO_2 + 2e^-$

Total electrons lost per mole of $FeC_2O_4$ is $1 + 2 = 3$. Thus, the n-factor of $FeC_2O_4$ is $3$.

Using the law of equivalence:
Equivalents of $K_2Cr_2O_7$ = Equivalents of $FeC_2O_4$

$x \times 6 = 1 \times 3$

$x = \dfrac{3}{6} = 0.5$

Answer: $0.5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the redox reaction, taking place in acidic medium:
$\text{X}\ \text{MnO}_4^-\ (aq) + \text{Y}\ \text{SO}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{+2}(aq) + \text{HSO}_4^-\ (aq)$,
the ratio of X:Y in a stoichiometrically balanced equation will be
questions.solution:
The given redox reaction can be balanced by splitting it into two half-reactions.

Reduction half-reaction:
$\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{+2} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Oxidation half-reaction:
$\text{SO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{HSO}_4^- + 3\text{H}^+ + 2e^-$

To equalize the number of electrons transferred, multiply the reduction half-reaction by $2$ and the oxidation half-reaction by $5$:

$2\text{MnO}_4^- + 16\text{H}^+ + 10e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{+2} + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$
$5\text{SO}_2 + 10\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 5\text{HSO}_4^- + 15\text{H}^+ + 10e^-$

Adding the two balanced half-reactions, we get the overall balanced equation:
$2\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{SO}_2 + \text{H}^+ + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{+2} + 5\text{HSO}_4^-$

Comparing this with the given equation $\text{X}\ \text{MnO}_4^- + \text{Y}\ \text{SO}_2 \rightarrow \dots$, we find:
$\text{X} = 2$
$\text{Y} = 5$

Therefore, the ratio of $\text{X}:\text{Y}$ is $2:5$.

Answer: $2:5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the law which is stated as "For any solutions, the partial vapour pressure of each volatile component in the solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction".
questions.solution:
Raoult's law states that for a solution of volatile liquids, the partial vapour pressure of each component of the solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction present in solution.

$p_i \propto x_i \Rightarrow p_i = p_i^0 x_i$

Gay-Lussac's law relates the pressure and temperature of a fixed mass of gas at constant volume.

Dalton's law states that the total pressure exerted by a mixture of non-reacting gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of individual gases.

Henry's law states that the partial pressure of the gas in vapour phase is proportional to the mole fraction of the gas in the solution.

Answer: Raoult's law

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The system that forms maximum boiling azeotrope is:
questions.solution:
A maximum boiling azeotrope is formed by solutions showing a large negative deviation from Raoult's law.

In an acetone-chloroform mixture, hydrogen bonding occurs between the oxygen atom of acetone and the hydrogen atom of chloroform. This makes the intermolecular attractive forces between the two different molecules stronger than those in the pure liquids.

As a result, the vapor pressure of the solution decreases, leading to a negative deviation from Raoult's law and the formation of a maximum boiling azeotrope.

Ethyl alcohol-water and carbon disulphide-acetone show positive deviations (minimum boiling azeotropes), while benzene-toluene forms an ideal solution.

Answer: Acetone-chloroform

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 1 mole of benzene is mixed with 1 mole of toluene, the vapours will contain
options: Equal number of moles of benzene and toluene since it is an ideal solution
Equal mass of benzene and toluene since it is an ideal solution
questions.solution:
Benzene is more volatile than toluene, which means the vapour pressure of pure benzene is greater than that of pure toluene ($P^{\circ}_B \gt P^{\circ}_T$).

Given that $1$ mole of benzene is mixed with $1$ mole of toluene, the mole fractions in the liquid phase are $x_B = 0.5$ and $x_T = 0.5$.

According to Raoult's law, the partial pressures in the vapour phase are $P_B = x_B P^{\circ}_B$ and $P_T = x_T P^{\circ}_T$.

Since $P^{\circ}_B \gt P^{\circ}_T$ and $x_B = x_T$, it follows that $P_B \gt P_T$.

By Dalton's law of partial pressures, the mole fraction in the vapour phase is $y = \dfrac{P}{P_{\text{total}}}$.

Therefore, $y_B \gt y_T$, meaning the vapour phase will contain a higher percentage of benzene.

Answer: Higher percentage of benzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A 5% solution (by mass) of cane sugar in water has a freezing point of 271 K. The freezing point of a 5% solution (by mass) of glucose in water is:
[freezing point of pure water: 273.15 K]
questions.solution:
Depression in freezing point is given by $\Delta T_{f} = K_{f} m$

For $5\%$ (by mass) cane sugar solution:

Mass of cane sugar $= 5$ g, Mass of water $= 95$ g

Molar mass of cane sugar $= 342$ g/mol

$\Delta T_{f1} = 273.15 - 271 = 2.15$ K

$2.15 = K_{f} \times \dfrac{5 \times 1000}{342 \times 95}$

For $5\%$ (by mass) glucose solution:

Mass of glucose $= 5$ g, Mass of water $= 95$ g

Molar mass of glucose $= 180$ g/mol

$\Delta T_{f2} = K_{f} \times \dfrac{5 \times 1000}{180 \times 95}$

Taking the ratio of $\Delta T_{f2}$ and $\Delta T_{f1}$:

$\dfrac{\Delta T_{f2}}{2.15} = \dfrac{342}{180} = 1.9$

$\Delta T_{f2} = 2.15 \times 1.9 = 4.085$ K

Freezing point of glucose solution $= 273.15 - 4.085 = 269.065$ K $\approx 269$ K

Answer: 269 K

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many molecules of C$O_2$(g) are obtained on reaction of 24 grams of methane with 4moles of oxygen?
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the combustion of methane is:

$CH_4(g) + 2O_2(g) \rightarrow CO_2(g) + 2H_2O(l)$

Molar mass of $CH_4 = 16 \text{ g/mol}$

Moles of $CH_4 = \dfrac{24}{16} = 1.5 \text{ moles}$

Moles of $O_2$ given $= 4 \text{ moles}$

From the stoichiometry, $1 \text{ mole}$ of $CH_4$ requires $2 \text{ moles}$ of $O_2$. Thus, $1.5 \text{ moles}$ of $CH_4$ require $3 \text{ moles}$ of $O_2$. Since $4 \text{ moles}$ of $O_2$ are available, $CH_4$ is the limiting reagent.

Moles of $CO_2$ produced $=$ Moles of $CH_4$ reacted $= 1.5 \text{ moles}$

Number of molecules of $CO_2 = 1.5 \times N_A = 1.5 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 9.033 \times 10^{23}$

Answer: $9.033 \times 10^{23}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 500 mL of an aqueous solution of glucose $C_6$H_{12}$O_6$ (Molar mass 180 gmol$^{-1}$) contains $6.02 \times 10^{22}$ molecules. The concentration of the solution will be:
questions.solution:
Number of moles of glucose is given by the ratio of the number of molecules to Avogadro's number.

$n = \dfrac{6.02 \times 10^{22}}{6.02 \times 10^{23}} = 0.1$ mol

Volume of the solution is $V = 500$ mL $= 0.5$ L.

Molarity is the number of moles of solute per liter of solution.

$M = \dfrac{n}{V} = \dfrac{0.1}{0.5} = 0.2$ M

Answer: $0.2$ M

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The frequency of photon which is emitted during a transition of electron of He$^+$ ion from fifth energy level to third energy level will be:
questions.solution:
Using the Rydberg formula for the frequency of the emitted photon:

$ u = R c Z^2 \left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} ight)$

For the He$^+$ ion, $Z = 2$. The transition is from $n_2 = 5$ to $n_1 = 3$.

$ u = R c (2)^2 \left( \dfrac{1}{3^2} - \dfrac{1}{5^2} ight)$

$ u = R c imes 4 imes \left( \dfrac{1}{9} - \dfrac{1}{25} ight)$

$ u = R c imes 4 imes \dfrac{16}{225} = R c imes \dfrac{64}{225}$

Substituting the values $R \approx 1.097 imes 10^7 ext{ m}^{-1}$ and $c = 3 imes 10^8 ext{ m/s}$:

$ u = (1.097 imes 10^7) imes (3 imes 10^8) imes \dfrac{64}{225}$

$ u = 3.291 imes 10^{15} imes 0.2844$

$ u \approx 9.36 imes 10^{14} ext{ s}^{-1}$

This value is closest to $9.39 imes 10^{14} ext{ s}^{-1}$.

Answer: $9.39 imes 10^{14}\ s^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statement is correct?
options: Azimuthal Quantum number explains about spatial orientation of orbital
Heisenberg uncertainty principle can be applied to all the objects and for macroscopic objects the uncertainty is extremely large
Photon has momentum as well as wavelength, but electrons do not have momentum and wavelength
In photoelectric effect if frequency $\nu  \gt  \nu_o$, then photoelectrons are ejected with certain kinetic energy
questions.solution:
The azimuthal quantum number ($l$) describes the shape of the orbital, whereas the magnetic quantum number ($m_l$) describes the spatial orientation of the orbital. Thus, the first statement is incorrect.

The Heisenberg uncertainty principle applies to all objects, but for macroscopic objects, the mass is large, making the uncertainty in position and velocity extremely small and negligible. Thus, the second statement is incorrect.

According to the de Broglie hypothesis, all material particles in motion, including electrons, possess both momentum and wavelength ($\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p}$). Thus, the third statement is incorrect.

In the photoelectric effect, if the frequency of incident light $ u$ is greater than the threshold frequency $ u_o$, the photoelectrons are ejected with a certain kinetic energy given by Einstein's photoelectric equation: $K.E. = h( u - u_o)$. Thus, the fourth statement is correct.

Answer: In photoelectric effect if frequency $ u \gt u_o$, then photoelectrons are ejected with certain kinetic energy

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the INCORRECT statement
options: A process will always be spontaneous at all temperatures, if T$\Delta$S is positive
For spontaneous process $([\Delta H_{system} - T\Delta S_{system}]) \lt  0$
At 273K, for the transition Ice$(s) \longrightarrow$ Water $(l)$, $\Delta$G = 0
Entropy is an extensive property and state function
questions.solution:
$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$

For a process to be spontaneous at all temperatures, $\Delta G$ must be negative at all temperatures. This is possible only when $\Delta H \lt 0$ and $\Delta S \gt 0$. If $\Delta S \gt 0$ (meaning $T\Delta S$ is positive) but $\Delta H \gt 0$, the process will be non-spontaneous at low temperatures where $\Delta H \gt T\Delta S$. Thus, a positive $T\Delta S$ alone does not guarantee spontaneity at all temperatures.

For a spontaneous process at constant temperature and pressure, $\Delta G_{system} = \Delta H_{system} - T\Delta S_{system} \lt 0$.

At $273$ K, ice and water are in equilibrium, so $\Delta G = 0$.

Entropy is an extensive property as it depends on the mass of the system, and it is a state function as it depends only on the initial and final states.

Answer: A process will always be spontaneous at all temperatures, if T$\Delta$S is positive

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The standard enthalpies of formation of CH_4$(g), CO_2$(g) and H_2$O(l) are $-74.8$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, $-393.5$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ and $-285.8$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively. Then the enthalpy change for the given reaction in kJ mol$^{-1}$ will be: \\ $2\text{CH}_4(g) + 4\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2(g) + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)
questions.solution:
The enthalpy of reaction is calculated using the standard enthalpies of formation of the products and reactants.

$\Delta_{r}H^{\circ} = \sum \Delta_{f}H^{\circ}(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta_{f}H^{\circ}(\text{reactants})$

For the given reaction:

$\Delta_{r}H^{\circ} = [2 \Delta_{f}H^{\circ}(\text{CO}_{2}) + 4 \Delta_{f}H^{\circ}(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})] - [2 \Delta_{f}H^{\circ}(\text{CH}_{4}) + 4 \Delta_{f}H^{\circ}(\text{O}_{2})]$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta_{r}H^{\circ} = [2(-393.5) + 4(-285.8)] - [2(-74.8) + 4(0)]$

$\Delta_{r}H^{\circ} = [-787.0 - 1143.2] - [-149.6]$

$\Delta_{r}H^{\circ} = -1930.2 + 149.6 = -1780.6 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-1780.6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal change, there is
options: an increase in Internal energy of the system and heat absorbed by the system is greater than the work done on the system
no change in Internal energy of the system and heat absorbed by the system is equal to the work done by the system
no change in Internal energy of the system and heat released by the system is equal to the work done by the system
a decrease in Internal energy of the system and heat released by the system is equal to the work done by the system
questions.solution:
For an ideal gas, the internal energy depends only on its temperature.

In an isothermal process, the temperature remains constant ($\Delta T = 0$).

Therefore, the change in internal energy is zero ($\Delta U = 0$).

According to the first law of thermodynamics:

$\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$

Substituting $\Delta U = 0$, we get:

$\Delta Q = \Delta W$

This implies that the heat absorbed by the system ($\Delta Q$) is equal to the work done by the system ($\Delta W$).

Answer: no change in Internal energy of the system and heat absorbed by the system is equal to the work done by the system

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x) = x^3 + \dfrac{3}{2}x^2 + 3x + 3$, then $f(x)$ is
questions.solution:
Given function is $f(x) = x^3 + \dfrac{3}{2}x^2 + 3x + 3$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = 3x^2 + 3x + 3$

$f'(x) = 3(x^2 + x + 1)$

The discriminant of the quadratic $x^2 + x + 1$ is $D = 1^2 - 4(1)(1) = -3 \lt 0$.

Since the leading coefficient is positive and $D \lt 0$, $x^2 + x + 1 \gt 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

Therefore, $f'(x) \gt 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

This implies that $f(x)$ is an increasing function.

Answer: Increasing function

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: An open hemispherical storage tank has radius 13 m. Oil flows into the tank such that the depth '$h$' of oil in the tank changes at the rate of 3 m / hr. When the depth $h = 1$m, the rate of change of the area of the top surface of the oil is
questions.solution:
Let $R$ be the radius of the hemispherical tank, so $R = 13$ m.

Let $r$ be the radius of the top surface of the oil at depth $h$. The distance from the center of the hemisphere to the oil surface is $R - h$.

Using the Pythagorean theorem in the cross-section of the hemisphere:

$r^2 + (R - h)^2 = R^2$

$r^2 = R^2 - (R^2 - 2Rh + h^2) = 2Rh - h^2$

The area of the top surface of the oil is $A = \pi r^2$.

$A = \pi(2Rh - h^2)$

Differentiating with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \pi(2R - 2h)\dfrac{dh}{dt}$

Given $R = 13$ m, $h = 1$ m, and $\dfrac{dh}{dt} = 3$ m/hr, substituting these values gives:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \pi(2(13) - 2(1))(3)$

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \pi(26 - 2)(3)$

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 72\pi$ m$^2$/hr

Answer: $72\pi$ m$^2$ / hr

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The function $f(x) = e^{ax} + e^{-ax}$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a \lt  0$, is strictly decreasing for all values of '$x$', where
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = e^{ax} + e^{-ax}$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = a e^{ax} - a e^{-ax} = a(e^{ax} - e^{-ax})$

For $f(x)$ to be strictly decreasing, $f'(x) \lt 0$.

$a(e^{ax} - e^{-ax}) \lt 0$

Since $a \lt 0$, dividing by $a$ reverses the inequality:

$e^{ax} - e^{-ax} \gt 0$

$e^{ax} \gt e^{-ax}$

Since the exponential function is strictly increasing, we can compare the exponents:

$ax \gt -ax$

$2ax \gt 0$

Since $a \lt 0$, dividing by $2a$ reverses the inequality again:

$x \lt 0$

Therefore, the function is strictly decreasing for $x \lt 0$.

Answer: $x \lt 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A movie screen on a wall is 20 feet high and 10 feet above the floor. What is the maximum viewing angle $\theta$ (in radians) that can be achieved by positioning yourself at the optimal distance from the wall?
questions.solution:
Let $x$ be the distance of the observer from the wall.

Let $\alpha$ be the angle of elevation to the bottom of the screen and $\beta$ be the angle of elevation to the top of the screen.

The height of the bottom of the screen is $10$ feet and the height of the top of the screen is $10 + 20 = 30$ feet.

From the geometry of the setup, we have $\tan \alpha = \dfrac{10}{x}$ and $\tan \beta = \dfrac{30}{x}$.

The viewing angle is $\theta = \beta - \alpha$.

$\tan \theta = \tan(\beta - \alpha) = \dfrac{\tan \beta - \tan \alpha}{1 + \tan \beta \tan \alpha}$

Substituting the values, we get:

$\tan \theta = \dfrac{\dfrac{30}{x} - \dfrac{10}{x}}{1 + \left(\dfrac{30}{x}\right)\left(\dfrac{10}{x}\right)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{20}{x}}{\dfrac{x^2 + 300}{x^2}} = \dfrac{20x}{x^2 + 300}$

To maximize $\theta$, we must maximize $\tan \theta$ since $\theta$ is an acute angle.

$\tan \theta = \dfrac{20}{x + \dfrac{300}{x}}$

Using the AM-GM inequality for $x \gt 0$, the minimum value of the denominator is:

$x + \dfrac{300}{x} \ge 2\sqrt{x \cdot \dfrac{300}{x}} = 2\sqrt{300} = 20\sqrt{3}$

The maximum value of $\tan \theta$ is therefore $\dfrac{20}{20\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

This maximum occurs when $x = \dfrac{300}{x} \Rightarrow x = 10\sqrt{3}$ feet.

Thus, $\tan \theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The absolute maximum and minimum values of the function $f(x) = \sin x + \sqrt{3}\cos x$ in $[0, \pi]$ are
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = \sin x + \sqrt{3}\cos x$

We can rewrite the function as:

$f(x) = 2 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \sin x + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cos x \right) = 2 \sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$

For $x \in [0, \pi]$, the angle $\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) \in \left[\dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right]$.

The maximum value of $\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ in this interval is $1$, which occurs at $x + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Thus, the absolute maximum value of $f(x)$ is $2 \times 1 = 2$.

The minimum value of $\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ in this interval occurs at the endpoint $x + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3} \Rightarrow x = \pi$.

Thus, the absolute minimum value of $f(x)$ is $2 \sin\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right) = 2 \left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -\sqrt{3}$.

Alternatively, evaluating the function at the critical point $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and the endpoints $x = 0, \pi$:

$f(0) = \sqrt{3}$

$f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = 2$

$f(\pi) = -\sqrt{3}$

Therefore, the absolute minimum value is $-\sqrt{3}$ and the absolute maximum value is $2$.

Answer: Minimum value $= -\sqrt{3}$, maximum value $= 2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Find the area bounded by the curve $y = |2 - x|$, the $x$–axis, and the lines $x = 0$ and $x = 5$
questions.solution:
The required area is given by the definite integral of $y = |2 - x|$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 5$.

$A = \int_{0}^{5} |2 - x| dx$

Since $|2 - x| = 2 - x$ for $x \le 2$ and $|2 - x| = x - 2$ for $x \ge 2$, the integral is split at $x = 2$.

$A = \int_{0}^{2} (2 - x) dx + \int_{2}^{5} (x - 2) dx$

Evaluating the first integral:

$\int_{0}^{2} (2 - x) dx = \left[ 2x - \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{2} = (4 - 2) - 0 = 2$

Evaluating the second integral:

$\int_{2}^{5} (x - 2) dx = \left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2} - 2x \right]_{2}^{5} = \left( \dfrac{25}{2} - 10 \right) - (2 - 4) = 2.5 - (-2) = 4.5$

Total area $= 2 + 4.5 = 6.5$ sq units.

Answer: $6.5$ sq units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area enclosed by the curve $y = -x^2$ and the line $x + y + 2 = 0$ is
questions.solution:
Find the points of intersection of the curve $y = -x^2$ and the line $x + y + 2 = 0$.

Substituting $y = -x^2$ into the line equation:

$x - x^2 + 2 = 0$

$x^2 - x - 2 = 0$

$(x - 2)(x + 1) = 0$

The points of intersection are at $x = -1$ and $x = 2$.

In the interval $[-1, 2]$, the parabola $y = -x^2$ lies above the line $y = -x - 2$.

The required area is given by:

$A = \int_{-1}^{2} [(-x^2) - (-x - 2)] dx$

$A = \int_{-1}^{2} (-x^2 + x + 2) dx$

$A = \left[ -\dfrac{x^3}{3} + \dfrac{x^2}{2} + 2x \right]_{-1}^{2}$

$A = \left( -\dfrac{8}{3} + \dfrac{4}{2} + 4 \right) - \left( \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2} - 2 \right)$

$A = \left( 6 - \dfrac{8}{3} \right) - \left( \dfrac{5}{6} - 2 \right)$

$A = \dfrac{10}{3} - \left( -\dfrac{7}{6} \right)$

$A = \dfrac{20}{6} + \dfrac{7}{6} = \dfrac{27}{6} = 4.5$ sq units.

Answer: $4.5$ sq units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A student needs to buy notebooks ($n$) for a semester. Double the number of notebooks plus 5 must strictly exceed 15, but the number of notebooks plus 10 must be no more than 22. What is the range of notebooks they can buy?
questions.solution:
From the first condition, double the number of notebooks plus $5$ strictly exceeds $15$:

$2n + 5 \gt 15$

$2n \gt 10$

$n \gt 5$

From the second condition, the number of notebooks plus $10$ is no more than $22$:

$n + 10 \le 22$

$n \le 12$

Combining the two inequalities, we get $5 \lt n \le 12$.

Since the number of notebooks must be an integer, the possible values for $n$ are $6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12$.

The set of possible values is $\{6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12\}$.

Answer: $\{6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12\}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\binom{n}{13}$, $\binom{n}{14}$ and $\binom{n}{15}$ are in arithmetic progression, then the positive integer value of '$n$' can be
questions.solution:
Given $^{n}C_{13}$, $^{n}C_{14}$, and $^{n}C_{15}$ are in arithmetic progression.

$2 \times \binom{n}{14} = \binom{n}{13} + \binom{n}{15}$

Dividing the equation by $^{n}C_{14}$, we get:

$2 = \dfrac{^{n}C_{13}}{^{n}C_{14}} + \dfrac{^{n}C_{15}}{^{n}C_{14}}$

Using the property $\dfrac{^{n}C_{r}}{^{n}C_{r-1}} = \dfrac{n-r+1}{r}$, we have:

$2 = \dfrac{14}{n-13} + \dfrac{n-14}{15}$

Multiplying by $15(n-13)$ on both sides:

$30(n-13) = 14 \times 15 + (n-14)(n-13)$

$30n - 390 = 210 + n^2 - 27n + 182$

$n^2 - 57n + 782 = 0$

$(n-23)(n-34) = 0$

$n = 23$ or $n = 34$

From the given options, $n = 34$.

Answer: $34$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the coefficients of $x^2$ and $x^3$ in the expansion of $(3 + kx)^9$ are equal, then the value of '$k$' is
questions.solution:
The general term in the expansion of $(3 + kx)^9$ is $T_{r+1} = ^{9}C_{r} (3)^{9-r} (kx)^r$.

For the coefficient of $x^2$, we put $r = 2$:
Coefficient of $x^2 = ^{9}C_{2} (3)^{7} k^2$

For the coefficient of $x^3$, we put $r = 3$:
Coefficient of $x^3 = ^{9}C_{3} (3)^{6} k^3$

Given that the coefficients are equal:
$^{9}C_{2} (3)^{7} k^2 = ^{9}C_{3} (3)^{6} k^3$

$\dfrac{9 \times 8}{2} \times 3 = \dfrac{9 \times 8 \times 7}{3 \times 2} \times k$

$36 \times 3 = 84 \times k$

$108 = 84k$

$k = \dfrac{108}{84} = \dfrac{9}{7}$

Answer: $\dfrac{9}{7}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The conjugate of the multiplicative inverse of the complex number $z = \dfrac{1 + 7i}{3 + i}$ is:
questions.solution:
$z = \dfrac{1 + 7i}{3 + i}$

Multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

$z = \dfrac{(1 + 7i)(3 - i)}{(3 + i)(3 - i)}$

$z = \dfrac{3 - i + 21i - 7i^2}{3^2 - i^2}$

$z = \dfrac{3 + 20i + 7}{9 + 1}$

$z = \dfrac{10 + 20i}{10} = 1 + 2i$

The multiplicative inverse of $z$ is $\dfrac{1}{z}$:

$\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{1}{1 + 2i}$

$\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{1 - 2i}{(1 + 2i)(1 - 2i)}$

$\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{1 - 2i}{1^2 + 2^2} = \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{2}{5}i$

The conjugate of the multiplicative inverse is:

$\overline{\left(\dfrac{1}{z}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{2}{5}i$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{2}{5}i$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The function $f(x) = |x| + |x - 1|$ is:
questions.solution:
The given function is $f(x) = |x| + |x - 1|$.

We can redefine the function as a piecewise function:

$f(x) = \begin{cases} -x - (x - 1) = -2x + 1, & x \lt 0 \\ x - (x - 1) = 1, & 0 \le x \lt 1 \\ x + (x - 1) = 2x - 1, & x \ge 1 \end{cases}$

Checking differentiability at $x = 0$:
Left Hand Derivative (LHD) $= \lim_{x \to 0^-} f'(x) = -2$
Right Hand Derivative (RHD) $= \lim_{x \to 0^+} f'(x) = 0$
Since LHD \neq RHD, $f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x = 0$.

Checking differentiability at $x = 1$:
Left Hand Derivative (LHD) $= \lim_{x \to 1^-} f'(x) = 0$
Right Hand Derivative (RHD) $= \lim_{x \to 1^+} f'(x) = 2$
Since LHD \neq RHD, $f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x = 1$.

Therefore, the function is neither differentiable at $x = 0$ nor at $x = 1$.

Answer: Neither differentiable at $x = 0$ nor $x = 1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{3\sin x + 4\cos x}{\sin x + \cos x}\, dx =$
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{3\sin x + 4\cos x}{\sin x + \cos x}\, dx$

Using the definite integral property $\int_0^a f(x)\, dx = \int_0^a f(a-x)\, dx$, we get:

$I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{3\sin(\pi/2 - x) + 4\cos(\pi/2 - x)}{\sin(\pi/2 - x) + \cos(\pi/2 - x)}\, dx$

$I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{3\cos x + 4\sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}\, dx$

Adding the two equations for $I$:
